name: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd
summary: Basran grammarian and lexicographer, the first and eldest of the three grammarians called al-Akhfash; Sībawayh quotes him in al-Kitāb.
bio: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, called al-Akhfash ('the weak-eyed') and later al-Akbar, 'the eldest', to tell him from two later grammarians with the same nickname, belonged to the fourth Basran generation in al-Zubaydī. He learnt from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and collected words and usages from the Bedouin; Sībawayh, Abū ʿUbayda and al-Aṣmaʿī learnt from him, and al-Kitāb cites him by name. He died in 177/793.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 11 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
